title: Integral scalar extension preserves bounded constructible integral complexes
statement: Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, with $\ell\neq p$, and let $Y$ be a scheme. For every $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the integral scalar extension $K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$. Hence integral scalar extension restricts to an $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$.

source.place: last paragraph (the functor $-\otimes_EL:D^b_c(Y,E)\to D^b_c(Y,L)$ is defined on integral representatives, which presupposes this); also asserted in dag node lem-coef-integral-finite-extension ('This exact functor preserves the integral bounded constructible categories')

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, $k_E=R/(\varpi_E)$ and $k_L=S/(\varpi_L)$, with completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_Y$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] the residue fields are finite and both valuation rings are DVRs. The maps of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] induce $k_E\to k_L$: $\varpi_E\in\varpi_L S$. This is a unital map of fields, hence injective. Since $k_L$ is a finite set, successively adjoining a vector outside the span of the vectors already chosen terminates and gives a finite $k_E$-basis, say of length $d$. By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] choose $r\le s$ bounding the cohomology of all reductions of $K$, in particular $K_1=K\otimes^L_R k_E$; its cohomology sheaves are constructible. Only this first reduction and its bound will be used in the finite-level argument.

source.place: last paragraph; elementary residue-field preparation using the coefficient DVR theorem

proof.text:
Choose one K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms as in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For $m\ge1$ put $B_m=S/(\varpi_L^m)$ and $M_m=P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_m)_Y$, with the strict quotient transition maps. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] these complexes compute $K\otimes^L_R B_m$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $M_m$ is K-flat with flat terms over $(B_m)_Y$. Consequently, for $m\ge n$, derived reduction of $M_m$ to $B_n$ is computed by its ordinary tensor, and the map
$$(P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_m)_Y)\otimes_{(B_m)_Y}(B_n)_Y\longrightarrow P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_n)_Y$$
is an isomorphism of complexes. Its local tensor formula is $(p\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto p\otimes bc$, with inverse $p\otimes c\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes c$; balancing makes the maps inverse. The maps commute with differentials, and for $m\ge n\ge a$ both composites send $(p\otimes b)\otimes c\otimes z$ to $p\otimes bcz$. Thus the adjoints of the specified transition maps are these isomorphisms and satisfy the quotient cocycle. The strict system is a normalized DVR tower in the sense of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]; this establishes normalization rather than assuming it.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); explicit balanced tensor comparison and quotient cocycle

proof.text: Put $P_1=P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(k_E)_Y$. It represents $K_1$ by the definition of derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], $P$ being a K-flat resolution of $K$, and it is K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. The coefficient map to $(k_L)_Y$ factors through $(k_E)_Y$. The balanced chain maps $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$ and $p\otimes b\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes b$ identify $P_1\otimes_{(k_E)_Y}(k_L)_Y$ with $Q=P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(k_L)_Y$. Apply [lem-sf-finite-field-sheaf-scalar-extension] to the unital map of finite fields $k_E\to k_L$ from step 1 and the complex $P_1$. Its cohomology formula proves that $Q$ has constructible $k_L$-cohomology, zero outside $[r,s]$.

source.place: Tag 093V, lemma-tensor-product-locally-constant; residue-field extension lemma, applied after balanced tensor associativity

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$ and put $B_m=S/(\varpi_L^m)$. Filter $B_m$ by $J_j=\varpi_L^jS/\varpi_L^mS$ for $0\le j\le m$. Thus $J_0=B_m$ and $J_m=0$. Multiplication by $\varpi_L^j$ gives $k_L\cong J_j/J_{j+1}$ for $j<m$: surjectivity follows from the definition of $J_j$, and cancellation in the DVR domain $S$ shows that its kernel before passing to $k_L$ is $(\varpi_L)$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Starting at $J_m=0$, each fiber of $J_j\to k_L$ is a coset of the finite group $J_{j+1}$; descending induction proves each $J_j$, hence $B_m$, finite. Viewed through $B_m\to k_L$, $Q$ still has constructible cohomology as a $B_m$-complex: its local constant models are the same finite modules with the action restricted through that map, and its underlying cohomology sheaves and bounds do not change [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf].

source.place: last paragraph; elementary DVR ideal filtration and restriction of finite constant module models

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-filtered-coefficient-tensor-bounds] with $B=B_m$, $\mathcal R=\widehat R_Y$, the coefficient map $\rho_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], $V=B_m$, and $V_j=J_j$ from step 4. Its flat-term hypothesis holds for the fixed resolution $P$. Every layer $W_j$ is $k_L$ as a $B_m$-module, so its tensor complex is $Q$, whose constructibility and support in $[r,s]$ were established in steps 3 and 4. The theorem gives constructible cohomology of $P\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}(B_m)_Y=M_m$ with the same interval $[r,s]$. The integers $r,s$ were chosen once in step 1 and do not depend on $m$ or the filtration length. No flatness of $B_m$ over $A_{E,m}$ or finite Tor hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 09B5, lemma-constructible-serre; finite coefficient-filtration tensor bounds applied to the DVR ideal filtration

proof.text: Let $X_m=\operatorname{Res}^L_m M_m$, a strict tower of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-complexes. By [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], $N=K\otimes_R S$ is precisely $\operatorname{Roos}(X)$. Countable products in the category of these completed-coefficient module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Apply [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] to this ringed site and strict tower. It identifies the fixed cone $N$ with the total derived inverse limit of the coherent tower, compatibly with every evaluation $N\to X_m$. Thus the finite-level counit comparisons for this derived limit are comparisons for the actual object and evaluations defining integral scalar extension; no uniqueness of arbitrary cone maps is asserted.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products; strict Roos comparison with total derived inverse limit and evaluations

proof.text: Step 2 established the normalized-tower hypothesis of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] for $S=\mathcal O_L$ and its quotients $B_m$. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to this tower, using the evaluation-compatible derived limit identification in step 6. It gives $N\otimes^L_S B_m\cong M_m$ for every $m$ and derived completeness of $N$. Step 5 supplies constructibility of all these reductions and a single cohomological interval $[r,s]$. For the finite coefficient ring $B_m=A_{L,m}$, constructibility of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] is word for word the finite-torsion constructibility of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] (finite partition into locally closed constructible strata, locally constant restrictions with finite stalks), and cohomology in $[r,s]$ gives finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, so $N\otimes^L_SB_m\cong M_m\in D^b_c(Y,A_{L,m})$. By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], these are precisely the defining conditions for $N\in D^b_c(Y,S)$.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2 and the normalized DVR effectivity assertion of lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity; no effectivity is inferred from merely being a triangulated homotopy limit

proof.text: The ambient integral scalar-extension functor is $R$-linear by clause 3 of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Step 7 shows that it sends every object of the integral bounded constructible full subcategory into the corresponding full subcategory for $S$. Restrict its object and morphism maps to these full subcategories. The equality $T(af)=aT(f)$ on ambient morphisms is the same equality on their full-subcategory Hom groups. This is the asserted $R$-linear functor.

source.place: last paragraph; restriction of the already linear ambient functor to preserved full subcategories

proof.text: For the intrinsic Lean interface, identify IsSfDerivedComplete with the legacy K-flat augmented-tower predicate using lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison. The finite reduction functors are definitionally identical and the common support interval is the same condition. Choose a prime q greater than l and the datum with base field ULift(ZMod q); no structure on Y is introduced. Apply the already published legacy integralScalarExtension_constructible, which carries the preceding mathematical proof plan, then transfer the result back to sfIntegralConstructible.
